To highlight the extent of United’s woes, they have only won one of the last 10 matches. There have been five draws in that time though and four losses. Nonetheless, no United fan will need reminding that two of those defeats were by 7-0 and 4-0 scorelines. Marcus Rashford Rashford impressed in the first couple of games of the season but has had a return to Manchester to forget. He has not scored a goal since returning from Barcelona on loan and has missed a lot of football owing to injury. Nonetheless, he should be fit again to be in the squad this weekend and no player in the current team has scored more goals against Liverpool. He has a total of seven goals against the old rival and how he would love to bag another one at Anfield this Sunday. cb03cf9cf0ee1e29.title: Brighton are rocking the Premier League elite. But can they mount a title tilt?
cb03cf9cf0ee1e29.text: A combination of smart analytics, a young manager and players hand-picked for their particular skills has the Seagulls flying high
cb03cf9cf0ee1e29.content: They lined up in sky‑blue shirts, white shorts. A combined value of £327m. Enzo Fernández, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Elliot Anderson were starting their first match together in Manchester City’s midfield. But it was a Brighton midfielder who made the game’s first decisive contribution. Yasin Ayari slotted the ball home. The away crowd at the Etihad Stadium roared, then watched their team defend relentlessly, securing Brighton’s first league victory away to City. It was 31 October 2026. There are dangers in reading too much into a single result this early in the season. Teams are still finding their rhythm, new signings bedding in. But this result packed some punch. If spending decided football matches, Brighton & Hove Albion should not be competing with, let alone beating, Manchester City, who sign established stars for astronomical fees and wages. Erling Haaland is paid £525,000 a week. According to an independent commission, to circumvent the Premier League’s spending limits, which restrict a club’s losses, City artificially inflated their commercial revenues by £830m between 2009 and 2018. Brighton, by contrast, tend to buy potential, scouring the market for undervalued talent, often in less prominent leagues. After developing them and benefiting from their performances, the club sell them for profits. They paid just £3.5m for Ayari, offering him about £10,000 a week, and paired him in midfield with Chema Andrés and Pascal Gross, signed for a combined fee of less than £25m. The most remarkable thing about Brighton’s win was that it wasn’t really a shock. In September, they dismantled Arsenal, the Premier League champions and favourites for the title. As they prepare for Sunday’s match at Hull, they are second in the league, sandwiched between Arsenal and City, and have scored more goals than anyone else in the division. How, then, do Brighton excel on the pitch without haemorrhaging money? And is there a ceiling to what they can achieve? On a crisp late October morning, I drove to Brighton in search of answers. Deep inside the Amex, the club’s stadium, I met Paul Barber, Brighton’s CEO, a cheerful man who speaks with the calmness of someone with nowhere else to be. “Being the size of club that we are, we had to find a way of being competitive that was probably different to any of the other bigger clubs that we were aiming to compete with,” Barber said, “because their revenues are always going to be higher: bigger stadiums, more established sponsorship models, bigger stars, bigger brands.” Hours before Brighton beat City, Chelsea had beaten Manchester United. In their respective midfields were Moisés Caicedo and Carlos Baleba, whom Brighton had signed for a combined fee of less than £30m and sold for about £180m. “It’s those trading profits that are effectively the core of the Brighton model,” Barber explained. Most clubs recruit and develop talent, I pointed out, but few do it better than Brighton. Who, outside Ecuador, had heard of Caicedo before he signed for Brighton in 2021? Two years later, the world’s biggest clubs were competing for his signature. The same can be said of dozens of others, among them Marc Cucurella and Alexis Mac Allister. One diamond exits, another enters. Caicedo replaced Yves Bissouma in central midfield. Baleba replaced Caicedo. The same applies to the dugout. Before joining Brighton, Fabian Hürzeler was coaching St Pauli in Germany; before him, Roberto De Zerbi had been at Shakhtar Donetsk. Barber grinned. “There’s a myth that we have this secret supply of players,” he said. The explanation is Jamestown Analytics, a sports analytics company founded by the club’s owner, Tony Bloom, as an offshoot of Starlizard, the gambling consultancy he established in 2006. Just as Starlizard uses proprietary modelling to identify mispriced odds in betting markets, Jamestown uses algorithms to identify underdeveloped football talents. “They’re all out there,” Barber said. “The data just enables Brighton to home in on them faster and earlier.” When I asked for more detail about how the system works, Barber fiddled with his watch. Jamestown tracks a vast number of performance indicators for every player competing in professional football, many of which aren’t captured by other data providers. “Every action that players are taking on a football pitch is being looked at, measured and codified in some way,” he said. When the club identify a position to strengthen, they draw up a list of attributes for the ideal player. Some are universal to the position: a centre-back generally needs to be tall. Others depend on the specific coach and their style of football. Later, when I spoke to Hürzeler, the head coach, he explained that the data had to reflect the specific demands of his playing system. “A player needs to have some basic things that fit our style of play, so if a player doesn’t want to have the ball then it’s difficult to play in our team. If a player doesn’t want to press high then it’s difficult to play in our team. These are just two examples.” One reason Brighton recruited Luka Vuskovic in July 2026 was because Hürzeler wanted a mobile centre-back. Reflecting on the City match, Barber recalled seeing Vuskovic pushing “so far forward that you’d have thought he was a right midfielder”. It was the sort of mobility Hürzeler’s system demanded, and Jamestown had identified. ‘The numbers have to be right’ Before Brighton’s victory over City, I met Mike Cave, the club’s sporting director, at the Lowry hotel in Manchester. A few of the Brighton players wandered around in club tracksuits. Cave wore a suit and tie and his hair was slicked back. He was telling me it was a big day without saying it. Brighton’s recruitment advantage lies not simply in the quality and quantity of the data at their disposal, he said, but in their ability to interpret it and trust what it tells them. “You could have the best data in the world but if you’re not accustomed to using it, and if you’re not cle

a14efcba1b209dbb.title: 'We did everything': Berrada breaks silence on shock exit of Man Utd wonderkid
a14efcba1b209dbb.text: Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has revealed that the club did everything possible to convince JJ Gabriel to remain at Old Trafford. The highly rated youngster recently announced his departure from United amid reports linking him with a potential move to Real Madrid. Having only recently turned 16, Gabriel is already regarded as one […] Article written by Sanidhya Bhardwaj .
a14efcba1b209dbb.content: Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has revealed that the club did everything possible to convince JJ Gabriel to remain at Old Trafford. The highly rated youngster recently announced his departure from United amid reports linking him with a potential move to Real Madrid. Having only recently turned 16, Gabriel is already regarded as one of the brightest prospects in world football, making his impending exit a significant blow for the Red Devils. Speaking to Sky Sports in an exclusive interview , Berrada admitted that United had exhausted every possible avenue in an attempt to keep the teenager at the club. Berrada said: “We did everything. Absolutely everything. “Let’s not forget with JJ, he’s a very young boy with a lot of media attention around him. Our primary concern is his well-being. “Credit to the academy and people that have been here for many years, they helped him in his development. We still think this is the best place for him to continue his career and to grow. “This club has a very rich history and tradition of developing young players and giving them the opportunity, as we’re seeing this season with Shea Lacey. Obviously, Kobbie Mainoo has been doing well for us for a few years now – we’re not afraid of giving young players opportunities. “Obviously, him and his family have taken the decision to leave. We can only wish him the best. “We want players that want to be here, that feel being at Manchester United is a privilege.” United cannot be blamed for JJ Gabriel exit Gabriel announced his departure from United on social media, reportedly without informing the club beforehand. His family also reportedly kept him away from training sessions just days before he was expected to make his senior debut against Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup. Such developments raise questions about the family’s decision-making, particularly given the opportunities and support the youngster has received throughout his time at United. Gabriel undoubtedly possesses the potential to become one of the finest players in world football, with the talent to follow in the footsteps of Cristiano Ronaldo or Lionel Messi and become a generational superstar. United clearly recognised his enormous potential and were prepared to go to considerable lengths to support his development. The teenager regularly trained with the first team, held conversations with Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick, and was even given the opportunity to meet club legend Sir Alex Ferguson. United appear to have done everything within their power to provide Gabriel with the ideal environment to develop his talent and build a future at Old Trafford. However, the club cannot be expected to keep a player against his family’s wishes, particularly when they have seemingly made up their minds about pursuing a move to Spain. 7c99d4847618af38.title: Eva Olid: Man United Women boss provides injury boost ahead of Birmingham City match
7c99d4847618af38.text: Eva Olid provides fitness updates, assesses Birmingham City and praises Maya Le Tissier before Manchester United Women's trip. The post Eva Olid: Man United Women boss provides injury boost ahead of Birmingham City match appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
7c99d4847618af38.content: Manchester United Women defeated Everton 2-1 on Wednesday in the Players’ Cup to make it a record 13 matches unbeaten in all competitions. As they chase London City Lionesses for the third and final Champions League spot, Manchester United Women’s Catalan coach Eva Olid will be desperate for a win against Birmingham City. Olid was speaking to the press ahead of her side’s trip to England’s second city this Sunday. Fitness updates Commenting on the state of her side’s injury situation, she explained, “Anna Sandberg is back. She missed the last two games. Andrea (Medina) is out of the squad with a small injury, and we hope she will be back after the international break.” In-form striker Mared Griffiths is also out for personal reasons. Elaborating further on Medina’s injury, she explained, “she won’t be with the international squad because she needs two or three weeks of recovery for her ankle. We hope that after those two or three weeks, she can be back with the squad.” Unbeaten run Despite the Women’s team being on a record-breaking run, the Catalan coach explained that her side remained level-headed. She added, “we continue to be demanding and focus on the things we can improve. Not everything is perfect, so we need to keep learning and getting better. Hopefully, we can deliver a good 90-minute performance on Sunday.” Birmingham threat Commenting on Sunday’s opponents, Olid said, “they have played good football in moments. They have good tactics and patterns, and they are dangerous on the counter-attack. They also have individual quality and can hurt any team in the league. They have individual talent, particularly on the left, but they also work very hard as a team. It’s going to be a competitive match.” She also doesn’t believe that her side are necessarily favourites, claiming, “I don’t like being favourites because anything can happen in football. I think we play better when we are underdogs than when we are favourites. I prefer to say it’s a 50-50 match because anything can happen.” Youth One of Olid’s biggest philosophies is her trust in young players, and she explained that the Players’ Cup has been great this season for showcasing the young players’ talent. She explained, “as I say, I’m very open to that. Just because they are young doesn’t mean they won’t play in the league. If they show what they can do and take their chances, they have possibilities to play in the league. They are improving more and more, and you will see some of them in the league as well.” Maya Le Tissier praise Manchester United captain Maya Le Tissier scored a goal on her 150th appearance against Crystal Palace last weekend, and Olid was full of praise for the captain. She added, “I can only say good things about her. She’s incredible to coach because she’s so demanding. She never wants to stop learning, she asks questions, and she always gives everything. She’s a leader, and she’s very honest when she sees something isn’t working. 0a0a58c9a6b02dbe.content: Manchester United Women have unearthed another gem from the Carrington production line. This season has seen quite a few Women starlets prosper under Eva Olid’s guidance. The Players’ Cup has given the Red Devils the opportunity to field numerous youngsters including Jess Anderson, Lucy Newell, Layla Drury, Jessica Simpson and Emma Watson, who scored last time out versus Everton. Nonetheless, no young player has taken their chance more than Welsh starlet Mared Griffiths. She has bagged an incredible seven goals in five matches in the cup, including a hat-trick against Sheffield United. Griffiths looks destined to succeed and here is why she can emulate Ella Toone and become a home-grown inspiration. Right coach at the right time Former manager Marc Skinner was often criticised for his lack of faith in young players. One of the reasons Olid was appointed was her history of bringing through youth and she has so far lived up to that billing. Griffiths has seized the opportunity with both hands and will only continue to get chances under Olid as she has clearly won Olid’s trust. What’s more, Olid favours attacking football where her side is on the front foot looking to score and this suits an attacking-minded player like Griffiths. Speaking last month on her role under Olid she explained , “I really enjoy the way Eva wants us to play and she likes giving young players opportunities, which suits me. But we all understand that we have to work for those opportunities.” “She’ll put anyone on the pitch if she knows they’re going to give 100 per cent, and that’s what I’m willing to do.” Her next target will be getting more valuable minutes in the WSL matches. Talent Griffiths’ talent has shone through this season with greater trust and attacking emphasis. The Welsh woman is “a versatile, goal-oriented attacker—operating across the wing, attacking midfield, and up front—known for directness, sharp acceleration, and composure in front of goal.” Her composure in front of goal and pace around the box will always make her a threat and give her a chance to succeed as finding regular scorers is a challenge at any level of football. What’s more, the goals she has scored this season have demonstrated a mixture of pure poaching and also the ability to create her own shots and chances, only adding more strings to her bow as an attacker. International experience Griffiths has not only gained first-team experience from United. She is already an established Welsh international. The striker has four goals in 12 appearances for her national side, including three so far this calendar year. This demonstrates that she can handle the pressure of scoring goals for a senior side. Final thoughts No player is a guaranteed success and anything can happen in football. Nonetheless, United have unearthed a talent at Carrington who can follow in Ella Toone’s footsteps and be the attacking face of the club for years to come. 14ea90f39d7cd48a.title: 'Our intention is': Pochettino makes bold Man Utd promise before Liverpool clash
14ea90f39d7cd48a.text: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has sent a defiant message to supporters ahead of the crucial Premier League showdown against Liverpool. The Red Devils are preparing to travel to Anfield tomorrow to face their fiercest rivals in one of the biggest fixtures of the season. Pochettino will take charge of United for the first time […] Article written by Sanidhya Bhardwaj .
14ea90f39d7cd48a.content: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has sent a defiant message to supporters ahead of the crucial Premier League showdown against Liverpool. The Red Devils are preparing to travel to Anfield tomorrow to face their fiercest rivals in one of the biggest fixtures of the season. Pochettino will take charge of United for the first time since replacing Michael Carrick, with the new head coach facing an immediate test of his credentials. He said in an interview with Sky Sports : “We need to build step by step. Ofcourse, we want to create an impact but our intention and atitude is to go there and try to win. That is the most important thing. “Important is to play in a way from the beginning that we want to continue forward. It is going to be a good start in a game that is going to demand the best of us.” Pochettino aiming for a rare positive start Apart from his spell at Paris Saint-Germain, Pochettino has never reached double figures in points from his first six league games in charge. He collected just five points with both Southampton and Chelsea, while his Tottenham Hotspur side managed eight points during the same period. The 54-year-old has often needed time to implement his methods and help players adapt to his tactical demands. However, he cannot afford a prolonged settling-in period at Old Trafford, with United already languishing in 18th place after 10 Premier League matches. Liverpool will understandably start as favourites at Anfield, meaning even a draw could represent a valuable result for the struggling visitors. Nevertheless, Pochettino has no intention of approaching the contest with a defensive mindset and wants his players to believe they can take all three points. United have won just once at Anfield in the past decade, with that memorable victory coming last season under former head coach Ruben Amorim. The travelling supporters will undoubtedly welcome their new manager’s positive approach and his determination to take the game to Liverpool. Now, the challenge is for the players to respond to his message, show the required character and produce a performance capable of delivering a major upset. 273df0736f1bb789.title: Premier League resumes, Kane facing spell on sidelines: football news – matchday live
273df0736f1bb789.text: Join Dominic Booth for buildup to today’s games as the Premier League returns after the international break
273df0736f1bb789.content: Before I get onto Pochettino and United, I’ve just seen a highlights edit on Twitter X of Premier League wingers between 2015 and 2020: Rihad Mahrez, Leroy Sane, Mo Salah, Sadio Mane, Alexis Sanchez, Raheem Sterling … was that a truly golden age of wide men in the English top flight? Many of them were inverted, of course, but they were box office. It certainly feels like wingers are slightly less important now. Antoine Semenyo and Bukayo Saka are probably the leading men, but that sprinkle of star dust in wide positions has faded somewhat. Am I talking nonsense, or is there something in that argument? Pop me or the matchday live address an email. Find more Premier League news in The Talk. This week it includes bits from David Moyes on Jack Grealish and Andoni Iraola on Liverpool’s clash with Manchester United, as well as more from Alonso and Maresca. Enzo Maresca has said he may need to tweak the balance of Manchester City’s midfield. City have suffered three consecutive defeats in the league, having begun the campaign with seven wins on the bounce, and are third in the table, six points off leaders Arsenal, and face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium at lunchtime today. Maresca defended Enzo Fernández, whose performances have prompted debate over his best position and whether he leaves City’s team unbalanced. “For sure there are things we need to do better in terms of balance,” Maresca said. “But the same midfield that won seven games in a row is the same midfield that lost three games in a row. “We won games with Enzo, we lost games with Enzo. I know that when there is a defeat, we are all looking for the reason why. Sometimes we probably need more balance, we need different kinds of players. [It] depends a little bit on the game. The idea is to continue in attack in the same way, creating chances, but finding a balance when we defend.” Xabi Alonso has admitted Chelsea’s injury list is a concern. The club have a lighter schedule after their failure to qualify for Europe but are struggling to keep players fit and have a host of selection issues before today’s home game against Leeds. João Pedro is yet to return from a thigh injury, Reece James is unlikely to recover from knee surgery until the new year and Maxence Lacroix is out with a long-term hamstring injury. Jorrel Hato and Jamie Gittens are also unavailable. “It’s a concern,” Alonso said of the injuries. “Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason. “I [have to] adapt to the circumstances. With the injuries you don’t have a choice. Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu.” Mauricio Pochettino was obviously the big draw on yesterday’s Premier League press conference callsheet, but there was some other news via some other more familiar faces in terms of this season’s managerial lineup. I’ll run through some of those news lines before pivoting to big Poch’s big United unveiling. Dominic here. Morning all. Let’s get straight into it, shall we? Bayern Munich and England were rocked by the news last night, confirmed by the Bundesliga champions, that will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted after 20 minutes and his Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, said the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal. Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired Cologne ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half in a further blow to Kompany’s men. Dominic will be here shortly ahead of a busy Saturday of Premier League and Women’s Super League action. The Premier League returns after the men’s international break with Manchester City hoping to get back on track after three consecutive defeats in the league when they host Fulham in today’s 12.30 kick-off (all times GMT). The afternoon kick-offs include Chelsea v Leeds, Spurs v Ipswich and Thomas Frank’s first match in charge as Crystal Palace take on Coventry. Then at 5.30pm, Arsenal head to Tyneside to take on Newcastle. Have a read of the latest Premier League news including Jack Grealish’s return after his recent disciplinary breach and Enzo Maresca’s plan for improving his side’s form. Plus, here is a video from Brighton on what their recruitment team look for when signing players. In the Women’s Super League Liverpool host the league leaders, Chelsea, before London City Lionesses take on Crystal Palace. During the week, Chelsea were made to work hard for three Champions League points against a resilient Paris Saint-Germain. Arsenal, meanwhile, had another wake up call against OL Lyonnes in their defeat at home. Here is an interview with Arsenal’s Lisa Baum, where she discusses her new life in London and drawing strength from the memory of her late brother, Dennis. Plus EFL, Scottish Premiership, European club football and more to look forward to. Join us, and if you have any thoughts, feel free to share below the line or at matchday.live@theguardian.com.

The Red Devils have let in 30 goals across competitions this season, including 19 in 10 games in the Premier League, where they have slipped to 18th in the table. The situation has prompted drastic actions from the club hierarchy – Michael Carrick has been removed from his position, while Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as his replacement. While there is optimism that the Argentine can pull the club out of dire straits, it is also evident that he will need backing in the transfer market to successfully implement his tactics. United need defensive reinforcements All signs indicate that defensive reinforcements will be at the centre of United’s transfer activity in 2027 and for good reason too. Harry Maguire is on the wrong side of 30 and out of contract at the end of this season. 238aaa0a0a5dd2fe.text: Manchester United have reportedly been made aware of a potential opportunity to re-sign former player Scott McTominay from Napoli in 2027. The post Scott McTominay: Man United offered chance to bring Napoli star back to Old Trafford appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
238aaa0a0a5dd2fe.content: Manchester United made the surprise decision to allow Scott McTominay to join Napoli in 2024, under former manager Erik ten Hag. The Red Devils replaced the Scot with Manuel Ugarte and it would turn out to be a disastrous decision. Brought in to replace Casemiro at Old Trafford, the Uruguayan was a disappointment, and soon became a peripheral figure at the Theatre of Dreams. Ugarte is currently sidelined after rupturing his ACL at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The Brazilian eventually left this summer with his head held high, and the English giants ended up spending over £150 million on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba to fill his boots. Unfortunately, the trio are yet to live up to the task, with United struggling to control the midfield in games and now sitting 18th in the Premier League table after 10 games. The situation has prompted talk of further reinforcements in the middle of the park in 2027, with rumours of a possible homecoming for McTominay refusing to go away. McTominay’s spectacular rise in Italy McTominay hit the ground running in Serie A, helping Napoli win the league in his debut campaign and finishing as the Serie A MVP. The 29-year-old was equally decisive last season, with his team finishing second behind Inter Milan. The Scottish midfielder’s spectacular rise in Italy has generated a very poor impression of United’s decision-making. Meanwhile, former manager Ten Hag has recently revealed that he was vehemently opposed to McTominay’s departure . The Scot’s contract expires in 2028 and he has yet to sign a new deal, adding to speculation regarding his future. It now, however, appears that the Red Devils could have the opportunity to rectify their error and bring their prodigal son home. Scott McTominay Stats for Man United Player Nationality Pos United career Apps Goals Scott McTominay Scotland MF 2017–2025 258 29 Source: Wikipedia and API-Football United alert to McTominay’s Napoli situation According to TEAMtalk , United could have the opportunity to bring their former academy graduate back in 2027. The report states: “Scott McTominay is heading into 2027 with one eye on a possible return to the Premier League, with former club Manchester United being made aware of an opportunity to bring him back to Old Trafford, TEAMtalk understands.” The report confirms that Napoli are keen to keep hold of McTominay, but adds that “the two parties remain some way apart in their negotiations, with no breakthrough currently in sight.” Intermediaries are already working on the player’s next move, with the report adding: “TEAMtalk can reveal that intermediaries are now working on potential options for McTominay heading into 2027, with a return to English football firmly among the possibilities being explored.” “Manchester United have been informed of his potential availability, and TEAMtalk understands the idea of bringing their former academy graduate back to Old Trafford has not been dismissed out of hand.” AC Milan, Juventus, Chelsea and clubs from Saudi Arabia are also hot on his heels, and the report states that the player would prefer a return to England. The Peoples Person Reliability Assessment Overall credibility: 5/10 Why? McTominay has been linked with a return to United for a while. This could be a ploy from the Scot’s agents to get Napoli to offer him a better contract. TPP view We believe that a cost-effective move for McTominay could tempt United, but the final decision regarding the matter will rest on new manager Mauricio Pochettino. cdd16770016bd483.title: United could sell award-winning teenager in January as West Ham circle
cdd16770016bd483.text: West Ham United are monitoring Manchester United left-back Harry Amass, who could reportedly leave Old Trafford in January amid uncertainty over his contract. The post Harry Amass could leave Manchester United in January as West Ham United circle appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
cdd16770016bd483.content: Harry Amass could leave Manchester United in January, with West Ham United said to be monitoring the 19-year-old left-back as his contract approaches its final months. Loan spells and a stalled route into United’s side United loaned Amass to Sheffield Wednesday in September 2025. He played 21 Championship matches, scored once and won consecutive club Player of the Month awards in November and December. Norwich City signed him for the remainder of the 2025/26 campaign in January, but a serious hamstring injury curtailed that spell after one substitute appearance. He returned to United for rehabilitation in April. Amass remained at Old Trafford beyond the latest summer window and has since played for the Under-21s. He also scored the winning goal for England Under-20s against Portugal during the November international break. West Ham track Amass as January decision approaches Former West Ham and United scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that the Hammers are among several clubs monitoring Amass. The outlet reports that a permanent January move could be considered if United fail to make progress in talks over a new contract. The defender has not appeared in the Premier League this season, although he has featured twice in the Champions League. United are said to rate him highly and retain significant hopes for his development, but his limited senior involvement has opened the door to another move. United were open to a loan during the summer transfer window and Wolves made contact, but those plans were reportedly halted after the club failed to add another left-back. Amass was instead retained as cover. Patrick Dorgu and Luke Shaw have both since moved closer to returning to action . Brown said: “Personally, I think he needs to play a bit more senior football before he’s ready for Man United, and that might be the club’s stance as well.” The former scout believes Amass’ reported contract situation makes another temporary spell difficult. He explained: “The thing is, his contract is up in the summer, so they’re not going to want to let him go on loan just to lose him for free at the end of the season if he doesn’t extend his deal.” Brown added: “In that case, it looks likely he could be allowed to leave in January for a fee so that they don’t let him go for nothing, and I’m sure there will be clubs interested.” Championship sides have also been linked with the teenager. West Ham want to strengthen at left-back after El Hadji Malick Diouf joined Brentford following their relegation from the Premier League. Head coach Scott Parker is reported to be planning several additions as he attempts to improve a squad expected to challenge for promotion. Brown said: “West Ham are certainly going to be keeping tabs on him, because it’s a position they want to strengthen in, and he’s already proved he can perform in the Championship.” From Watford prospect to United award winner Amass joined Watford’s academy at the age of nine before moving to Manchester United in July 2023 for an undisclosed fee. He helped the Under-18s win the national championship, northern title and Premier League Cup during the 2023/24 season. The left-back made his senior debut on his 18th birthday in a 3-0 Premier League victory at Leicester City in March 2025. He was subsequently named United’s Jimmy Murphy Young Player of the Year for 2024/25 and has made nine competitive first-team appearances without scoring. Final Thoughts West Ham are among several clubs monitoring Amass ahead of January. A permanent move could be considered if contract talks do not progress. Brown believes the defender needs more regular senior football. 25584ed81fea50fb.title: Manchester City v Fulham: Premier League – live
25584ed81fea50fb.text: Minute-by-minute report: Will City return to winning ways at home after a run of three successive league defeats? Join Barry Glendenning
25584ed81fea50fb.content: Alvaro Arbeloa: “I have watched all Manchester City games and the last three games that they lost I woudn’t say they were the worst team,” said Fulham’s head coach in yesterday’s press conference. “They have the chances. You can see the quality of the players, how they want to play. They are very, very aggressive when they lose the ball, so for me they are performing really, really well. “This is the Premier League, so you can feel how difficult every game is, but they won the first seven games, it was amazing. For me, they’re still one of the best teams in the world.” Asked about speculation linking Fulham defender Calvin Bassey with a move to Manchester United, Alvaro stressed the Nigerian international’s importance to the Cottagers. “He’s very, very important,” he said. “He is one of my captains. From the first days when I arrived I saw how good he is. I think he is one of the best centre backs in the world, so it’s normal if there are so many teams that wants Calvin, that for me is normal. “I’m not worried about that because I am really happy with Calvin. I think Calvin is really happy here. He is so important for us. He is one of our leaders.” Elsewhere in Manchester: Maine Road FC,who play in English football’s tenth tier, aim to become a new home for any Manchester City supporters disillusioned by the possible consequences of the guilty verdict handed down to their team, and those priced out of the Premier League. Dominic Booth reports … Gonzalo Garica: The Fulham striker and great nephew of Rita Hayworth admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he will remain calm over his 11-match goal drought. Interview: Sid Lowe. Today’s match officials Referee: Tom Bramall Assistants: Gary Beswick and Craig Taylor. Fourth official: Sam Barrott. VAR: James Bell. Assistant VAR: Adam Nunn. Those teams: Enzo Maresca makes three changes to the City team that started against Nottingham Forest last time out, with Nico O’Reilly, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Phil Foden coming into his side. Josko Gvardiol, Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki drop to the bench. Abdukodir Khusanov and Marc Guehi have both been selected despite missing out on international duty with Uzbekistan and England resepectively through injury. There are also three changes to the Fulham side that lined up against Newcastle before the international break. Kenny Tete, Ryan Sessegnon and Rodrigo Muniz have been selected today, with Timothy Castagne, Antonee Robinson and Gonzalo Garcia making way. Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly, Anderson, Bouaddi, Ndiaye, Foden, Doku, Haaland Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Cherki, Fernandez, Reis, Gvardiol, Allan, Samba, Lewis Fulham: Leno, Tete, Bassey, Affengruber, Sessegnon, Charles, Berge, Iwobi, King, Bobb, Muniz. Subs: Kaiser, Cuenca, García, Palacios, Cairney, Larsson, Angel, Castagne, Robinson. Early team news Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo remains sidelined with the knee injury he suffered against Ipswich in October, while defenders Marc Guehi and Abdukodir Khushanov have been rated doubtful for today’s game. Speaking at his press conference yesterday, Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa confirmed that reserve goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will be out for the season after rupturing his achillles tendon in a practice match played against West Ham behind closed doors during the international break. Midfielder Tom Cairney is struggling with a knee injury but could feature in today’s squad, while Emile Smith-Rowe is unlikely to be in the matchday squad as he has a hip injury. Following the second international break of the season, the Premier League resumes at the Etihad Stadium, with Manchester City hoping to halt a run of three consecutive defeats in the top flight. The most recent came against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground, where Liam Delap scored two quite extraordinary goals against the club where he learnt his trade. Fulham are unbeaten in four matches and came from behind to draw with Newcastle at Craven Cottage last time out. Rather astonishingly, they haven’t beaten Manchester City since 2009 and have lost 20 consecutive games against today’s hosts in an extraordinary run of defeats against the same opponents dating back to 2012. Kick-off at the Etihad Stadium is at 12.30pm (GMT) but we’ll have team news and buildup in the meantime.

156b159f95abb4b0.title: Ineos risk repeating a costly summer blunder as Man United’s January transfer stance emerges
156b159f95abb4b0.text: Manchester United risk repeating their left-back transfer mistake unless INEOS strengthen the position in the January window. The post Ineos risk repeating a costly summer blunder as Man United’s January transfer stance emerges appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
156b159f95abb4b0.content: Ask ten Manchester United fans which position they think INEOS must bolster this winter, and I bet more than half will point to left-back. Beyond midfield, left-back was the one position many felt required reinforcement. However, INEOS did not act, and the Red Devils have suffered as a result. Injuries to Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu , which coincided with October’s fixtures, have left the team without a natural left-back to rely on. As a result, Michael Carrick deployed makeshift left-backs to fill the gap. Opponents identified these options, such as Diogo Dalot , as a point of weakness and targeted them, exposing United. That said, even if Shaw and Dorgu were both back to full fitness, INEOS should still sign a top left-back; otherwise, they risk ending up in the same dilemma they faced in Carrick’s last few games. A left-back signing in the winter is not certain Yet it still seems the Red Devils have not learnt their lesson. They remain undecided about committing to a left-back transfer this winter, as the Manchester Evening News clarifies: “There are some holes in the squad that could be looked at, notably left-back and striker. Plans for the former will depend on Luke Shaw’s fitness and whether Patrick Dorgu emerges as an option in that position.” Luke Shaw 2026-27 stats Stat Premier League Competition Premier League Apps 5 Minutes 425 Starts 5 Sub appearances 0 Goals 0 Assists 1 Not signing a left-back in January will certainly elicit fans’ fury. How have INEOS not learnt? In the summer, they could have moved fast to capture their top target, Lewis Hall , early, when Newcastle were open to major sales. Instead, they waited until the Magpies no longer needed big sales, following the departures of Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, before trying to sign the left-back. Of course, Newcastle rebuffed the Red Devils’ approach. Even so, United could have pursued alternatives such as Alejandro Balde and Rayan Aït-Nouri , yet they never really made an effort. This failed transfer opportunity, and the struggles that followed in recent weeks, should have prompted United to sign a left-back in January. But no: almost a month before the window opens, it is still unclear whether the club will pursue that transfer. Risk of a summer repeat With Shaw back to his injury struggles and Dorgu also unable to stay fit this year, it would not be surprising if both were fit between now and February, only to return to the treatment table when needed most. Then United, in the final months of the 2026-27 season, could once again suffer for failing to act when they should have. 2feeeb0db0fc811f.title: Trabzonspor to start negotiations for United star available for free in the summer
2feeeb0db0fc811f.text: Trabzonspor are reportedly preparing talks to sign Andre Onana permanently as Manchester United seek funds for a squad rebuild. The post Andre Onana: Trabzonspor to start negotiations for United flop appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
2feeeb0db0fc811f.content: Mauricio Pochettino’s squad shake-up at Manchester United will depend largely on how much money he can raise in transfer sales, with the club desperately needing to improve in that area of the transfer market. The expenditure has far outweighed the incoming cash over the last decade, leaving United hamstrung when it comes to offering the big money for top stars that are moving to rivals both domestically and abroad. Another overhaul of players is expected in the next 12 months, with some high earners nearing the end of their lucrative Old Trafford contracts and underperforming or loaned-out players put up for sale to add to the kitty. Local media report the Turks are hoping to make the move a permanent one, with Onana seemingly doing enough to impress the figureheads at the club. The newly-appointed manager arrived at Carrington on Thursday after concluding his duties with the USMNT. 37a8abc922af9159.content: Mauricio Pochettino has called out the person who filmed his first Manchester United training session via a drone. The newly-appointed manager arrived at Carrington on Thursday after concluding his duties with the USMNT. Mauricio Pochettino awaiting first match in the dugout (Photo via MUTV) Pochettino oversaw the United States’ Concacaf Nations League double-header against Haiti, winning 8-0 on aggregate. He then flew straight to Manchester to kickstart his tenure with the Red Devils, giving him just three days of preparation before Sunday’s showdown against Liverpool at Anfield. Yet, his first day on the job was dampened by one nosey member of the public, as one YouTuber sent up his drone to spy on Pochettino’s maiden session with his squad. Over 12 minutes of footage was recorded, and an apology has since been issued. What did Pochettino have to say? (Photo via MUTV) However, Pochettino was – understandably – left infuriated by the incident. “Please, this guy, man. What are you trying to find?” the Argentine expressed. “We have young players training with us. It’s really not nice, and it’s not good. “What are you trying to show? Our training? That we’re working on our shape and that we’re very organised? “What’s the point of doing something that could be very dangerous? It’s something the club needs to deal with.” United return to action following the international break at 4.30pm tomorrow afternoon, where they’ll be looking to secure a second successive win on Liverpool’s home soil. Then, it’s an away encounter against Sporting Lisbon in matchday five of the Champions League. United sit 17th in the UCL standings, having won twice and lost twice since they got their campaign underway. Their most recent outing, which marked Michael Carrick’s penultimate game in charge, saw them come from 2-0 down to win 3-2, with all of their goals coming in the second half. 67a1208b37977d5b.title: Ineos risk repeating a costly summer blunder as Man United’s January transfer stance emerges

The post Ineos risk repeating a costly summer blunder as Man United’s January transfer stance emerges appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
67a1208b37977d5b.content: Ask ten Manchester United fans which position they think INEOS must bolster this winter, and I bet more than half will point to left-back. Beyond midfield, left-back was the one position many felt required reinforcement. However, INEOS did not act, and the Red Devils have suffered as a result. Injuries to Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu , which coincided with October’s fixtures, have left the team without a natural left-back to rely on. As a result, Michael Carrick deployed makeshift left-backs to fill the gap. Opponents identified these options, such as Diogo Dalot , as a point of weakness and targeted them, exposing United. That said, even if Shaw and Dorgu were both back to full fitness, INEOS should still sign a top left-back; otherwise, they risk ending up in the same dilemma they faced in Carrick’s last few games. A left-back signing in the winter is not certain Yet it still seems the Red Devils have not learnt their lesson. They remain undecided about committing to a left-back transfer this winter, as the Manchester Evening News clarifies: “There are some holes in the squad that could be looked at, notably left-back and striker. Plans for the former will depend on Luke Shaw’s fitness and whether Patrick Dorgu emerges as an option in that position.” Luke Shaw 2026-27 stats Stat Premier League Competition Premier League Apps 5 Minutes 425 Starts 5 Sub appearances 0 Goals 0 Assists 1 Not signing a left-back in January will certainly elicit fans’ fury. How have INEOS not learnt? In the summer, they could have moved fast to capture their top target, Lewis Hall , early, when Newcastle were open to major sales. Instead, they waited until the Magpies no longer needed big sales, following the departures of Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, before trying to sign the left-back. Of course, Newcastle rebuffed the Red Devils’ approach. Even so, United could have pursued alternatives such as Alejandro Balde and Rayan Aït-Nouri , yet they never really made an effort. This failed transfer opportunity, and the struggles that followed in recent weeks, should have prompted United to sign a left-back in January. But no: almost a month before the window opens, it is still unclear whether the club will pursue that transfer. Risk of a summer repeat With Shaw back to his injury struggles and Dorgu also unable to stay fit this year, it would not be surprising if both were fit between now and February, only to return to the treatment table when needed most. Then United, in the final months of the 2026-27 season, could once again suffer for failing to act when they should have. b83a6748f6817d7a.title: Elon Musk’s lawyer joining Tom Brady in buying Chelsea stake
b83a6748f6817d7a.text: Elon Musk’s lawyer Alex Spiro is joining the former NFL player Tom Brady in buying a stake in Chelsea
b83a6748f6817d7a.content: Elon Musk’s lawyer is joining Tom Brady in buying a stake in Chelsea. The Guardian revealed on Friday that the NFL player is in discussions about purchasing a minority shareholding at Stamford Bridge and can now disclose that Alex Spiro of the New York law firm Quinn Emmanuel is also seeking to buy a stake by investing in Chelsea’s majority owners, Clearlake Capital. Brady and Spiro, who is representing planned Fifa investor Joshua Kushner in a legal battle against Uefa, would become limited partners in Clearlake with no voting rights at Chelsea if the transactions are completed. Clearlake have been seeking additional investors since agreeing to buy the shares of former partners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter for around £1bn in September, a deal that is due to be completed by the end of the year. Clearlake will own 86.5% of Chelsea after buying out Boehly and Walter, who both held stakes of 12.9%, with the proposed investments of Brady and Spiro understood to be considerably smaller. As part of that transaction Boehly and Walter’s partner, the Swiss philanthropist Hansjorg Wyss, chose to stay at Chelsea by buying 12.9% of Clearlake’s shareholding. Any other future investors such as Brady and Spiro would follow the same model. Spiro has represented Musk since 2018 and advised on his $44bn (£33.6bn) purchase of Twitter (now X) in 2022, as well as working for other celebrity clients, including Alec Baldwin, Kim Kardashian and Jay-Z. In 2019 he successfully defended Musk in a notorious defamation trial relating to comments he made about the rescuer of junior football players from a Thailand cave, while in 2024 his defence helped Baldwin’s acquittal on charges involuntary manslaughter after a cinematographer died on the set of his film Rust, when a prop revolver discharged a live round. Last summer Spiro was also appointed to represent Kushner, whose company Thrive Capital were the lead investors in Gianni Infantino’s $4.2bn World Cup sell-off scheme, in a legal challenge from Uefa. Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, is facing court claims in the United States from Uefa’s lawyers to disclose all communications relating to Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise plan. Last week a New York court rejected a motion by two Fifa subsidiaries to dismiss Uefa’s claim, but the courts have yet to rule on the disclosure filing. Brady owned a 3.3% stake in Championship club Birmingham City until earlier this month, with sources involved in his decision to sell those shares telling the Guardian that he was paving the way to invest in Chelsea. The seven-time Super Bowl winner was a guest of Chelsea when they won the Club World Cup in New Jersey last year, and has a good relationship with the Clearlake’s main power broker, Behdad Eghbali, who has led discussions on behalf of the club. Brady bought into Birmingham in August 2023, less than a year after his second and final retirement from the NFL, following the club’s takeover by Tom Wagner’s Knighthead Capital. The 49-year-old was appointed chair of the club’s advisory board and had a prominent role in the 2025 Amazon Prime documentary Built in Birmingham: Brady & The Blues, which made headlines when he questioned the “work ethic” of Wayne Rooney, who was the manager. Brady also owns a minority stake in the NFL team the Las Vegas Raiders, which he bought alongside Wagner. Chelsea declined to comment.

a17ccfcbd6e4203d.title: Poch: We will win a lot of games
a17ccfcbd6e4203d.text: Mauricio Pochettino has praised the commitment of his Manchester United players and insisted that restoring their confidence will be crucial as he prepares for his first game in charge against Liverpool. The Argentine has wasted little time getting to know his new squad, revealing that he has already held individual conversations with almost every available […] The post Poch: We will win a lot of games first appeared on Republik Of Mancunia: A Manchester United Blog .
a17ccfcbd6e4203d.content: Mauricio Pochettino has praised the commitment of his Manchester United players and insisted that restoring their confidence will be crucial as he prepares for his first game in charge against Liverpool. The Argentine has wasted little time getting to know his new squad, revealing that he has already held individual conversations with almost every available player. He also emphasised the importance of Bruno Fernandes, although he was unwilling to discuss the captain’s contract situation just yet. I think the commitment of all the players, we were chatting, is amazing. Bruno is our captain and is a very important player. But all the players need to feel they are important, from the top to the bottom, or the bottom to the top. We were chatting yesterday, I spent three hours chatting in an individual way in my office with all the players. Maybe I miss some injured players. But, in the next few days, we will talk with everyone. It was a very nice contact, it’s important the players, to listen to what they need to say, to understand the place they are. It’s not only on the field, [it is] off the field [too], what is going on. But then [we had] some conversations in a collective way, some meetings but very focused to be ready for Sunday. Bruno is our captain and is a very important player. I think we will have time after to talk about the thing that you ask me [about his contract expiring]. For United supporters, one of the biggest frustrations has been watching talented players consistently underperform. Pochettino believes the ability is already there and that his responsibility is to help the squad rediscover it. It’s normal. When you don’t win games, it’s normal that the confidence starts to go down. I think the players need to feel something from us, like always happens with the new coaching staff, that you really believe and you really trust and then you need to show that you know what you are doing. That is the important thing. I think that the reception and the welcome in the last two days and the meetings and the training session, today we were talking at the end because I think it was a little bit longer the training session than it normally is on matchday minus two [two days before a game]. I said ‘thank you’ because they were able to make the effort. And I think that is good because with the scale that we have ahead, I think we need to find this bracket to try to settle our principles and, after, to apply our concept. And I think they are intelligent, they’re good players, they have the quality, it’s only [we need] to unlock [it]. Sometimes, it’s about unlocking things that maybe didn’t appear for different reasons. But that happened, it happens in all the coaching staff and all the clubs, it happened with us in the past. We learned a lot, like [I said] in the question before. We learned a lot and we try to unlock that because you cannot improve things [right away] that you need time [to improve]. But yes, if you are in a good level, you are happy, you have a great atmosphere, if you play together, if you have an organisation when you have the ball – the things that you need to do – and then when you don’t have the ball, fight together and also find your organisation. Simple things that can help, you know, to perform and after with the quality that they have, for sure we will win a lot of games. It is an encouraging message, although we have heard similar promises before. The challenge now is translating those words into performances, starting with Liverpool on Sunday. c6d33a4ba8d65ba1.content: Manchester United have reportedly renewed their interest in Victor Osimhen, with the Nigerian striker open to a move to Old Trafford as Mauricio Pochettino looks to strengthen his attacking options. According to reports, the 27-year-old is flattered by United’s interest and remains keen to play in the Premier League. However, securing his signature would be far from straightforward. Osimhen is contracted to Galatasaray until 2029, with the Turkish club reportedly demanding between £80million and £100million. He also earns approximately £13m a year, meaning United would need to make a significant financial commitment. With no release clause in his contract, Galatasaray are under no obligation to sell, particularly midway through the season. A summer transfer may therefore be more realistic. But would Osimhen be worth the investment? United’s struggles in front of goal make the appeal obvious. Benjamin Sesko and Joshua Zirkzee have managed just four goals between them this season, leaving us desperately short of a reliable goalscorer. Sesko has shown glimpses of real quality when fit but is proving to be a liability with his injury record. Osimhen certainly has the credentials to address the lack of goals. He scored 37 goals during his first season at Galatasaray, followed by 22 last season, and has already registered ten this campaign. His qualities extend well beyond his impressive goalscoring record. His intelligent movement and positional awareness allow him to find space in crowded penalty areas, while his anticipation frequently puts him in the right place to capitalise on rebounds and defensive mistakes. He is particularly effective at timing runs behind defenders and creating opportunities through clever changes of position. His finishing ability, understanding of teammates’ movements and tactical discipline when pressing opponents would also make him an attractive option for Pochettino. At 6ft 1in, Osimhen also combines physical strength with explosive pace, making him dangerous both inside the penalty area and when running behind defenders. Throughout his managerial career, the Argentine has favoured energetic, aggressive football, with forwards expected to press opponents and create space through intelligent movement. At Tottenham, Harry Kane became one of Europe’s finest strikers under Pochettino, although his role differed considerably from Osimhen’s. Kane developed into a complete centre-forward, dropping deep to link play and create opportunities for teammates. Osimhen is more of a traditional penalty-box striker, preferring to stretch defences with his pace and movement. There are also similarities with the role Pochettino gave Edinson Cavani at Paris Saint-Germain. Cavani’s intelligent runs, work rate and ability to attack space are qualities Osimhen possesses in abundance. At Southampton, Pochettino also enjoyed success with Rickie Lambert, another physical centre-forward, although Lambert relied more heavily on hold-up play and technical ability than explosive speed. Osimhen would offer something different from each of these players, but his attributes appear well suited to Pochettino’s preferred approach. The biggest question is whether United are prepared to spend another enormous sum on a striker, particularly after investing heavily in Sesko. There is also the issue of Osimhen’s recent knee surgery, which makes assessing his fitness important before committing such a substantial fee. Nevertheless, at his best, Osimhen is precisely the type of established, proven goalscorer United have been missing. Whether we can actually convince Galatasaray to sell him is another matter entirely. The post Could Osimhen Be the Perfect Striker for Pochettino? first appeared on Republik Of Mancunia: A Manchester United Blog .

76fc2b4e2002d894.title: "Scorched earth": sources expose Sir Jim Ratcliffe's concerning lack of football intelligence
76fc2b4e2002d894.text: Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS face fresh scrutiny over allegations about their leadership culture and its influence on Manchester United. The post “The cult of Sir Jim”: Ratcliffe’s concerning lack of football intelligence exposed by sources appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
76fc2b4e2002d894.content: Manchester United minority co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe is facing fresh scrutiny over claims that a hard-edged culture within INEOS has influenced the company’s approach to running the club. America’s Cup dispute preceded fresh scrutiny of INEOS INEOS partnered with Sir Ben Ainslie’s British America’s Cup team in April 2018, pledging £110 million towards the 2021 campaign. INEOS Britannia subsequently won the Louis Vuitton Cup in October 2024 before losing the America’s Cup final 7-2 to Emirates Team New Zealand. The parties separated in January 2025 and INEOS withdrew from the 2027 America’s Cup three months later. A legal dispute followed before the claim was settled on 16 November 2026. Discontent has also grown at Old Trafford, where four supporters recently received stadium bans after tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch during an ownership protest. United have maintained that they must take a strict approach because of the risks created by objects being launched from the stands, while fans have also objected to ticketing changes and the expansion of corporate seating. Claims of a ‘cult-like’ culture reach Old Trafford Court papers from the dispute over the £180 million yacht alleged that INEOS representative Raymond Fellows placed a chain and padlock on Athena Racing’s offices at Turweston Aerodrome after being refused the keys (via the Daily Mail ). Ratcliffe was also demanding the team’s assets and intellectual property. Ainslie and his financial officer Matt Robinson were inside and left through a fire escape. INEOS denied falsely imprisoning Ainslie, saying Fellows did not know anybody remained in the building and intended to stop people from entering. The company also pointed to the availability of alternative exits. Fellows had previously provided security assistance during protests at INEOS fracking sites. INEOS did not entirely challenge Ainslie’s account of a heated meeting involving Manchester United board member Rob Nevin. Ainslie claimed Nevin told him: “We have a phrase at Ineos: scorched earth. It means that if you don’t give Jim what he wants, he will burn your house down, or words to that effect.” The Mail says the “‘cult of Sir Jim’ is born of the billionaire’s own immense air of superiority and is something he seems to have instilled in some of his most senior executives.” Several unnamed sources also claim that senior employees fear challenging him. The report argues that the same approach has shaped INEOS’s football ventures, including the appointment of Bob Ratcliffe, Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s brother, as OGC Nice chief executive. Sir Jim is also said to have demonstrated his London Marathon stretches to United players and considered his friend, Sir Dave Brailsford , “best in class” for overseeing football matters despite his limited network within the game. Brailsford was so obsessed with Manchester City that he and other INEOS figures were allegedly “skipping around” after United recruited Omar Berrada . One anonymous source criticised the failure to prioritise established football expertise: “People like him see football on TV and just assume they can do it.” The criticism comes as INEOS reduces its wider sporting commitments. OGC Nice and FC Lausanne-Sport are reportedly available for sale, while “it is widely expected that Ineos will eventually disappear from cycling”. Legal disputes with the All Blacks and Tottenham Hotspur over terminated commercial agreements both ended in confidential settlements. Ratcliffe’s ownership record at Manchester United Manchester-born Ratcliffe, a lifelong United supporter, agreed his minority investment on 24 December 2023. The transaction was completed on 20 February 2024, initially giving him an ownership stake of approximately 27.7%, with INEOS taking responsibility for football operations. INEOS later increased its holding to 28.9% of the voting rights. Nevin and Reece joined Manchester United plc’s board when the original transaction was completed, while the club cut approximately 250 jobs in 2024 and announced plans for a further 150 to 200 potential redundancies in February 2025. Final Thoughts Ratcliffe and INEOS face allegations of a fearful, cult-like leadership culture. INEOS denied falsely imprisoning Ainslie and said the “scorched earth” remark was figurative. Senior figures at United are facing calls for more experienced football and boardroom support. Ainslie retained the disputed yacht after the legal settlement. a02ac80a3857578c.text: Liverpool are wary of Manchester United's visit to Anfield as Mauricio Pochettino prepares for his first match in charge. The post Andoni Iraola sweats on star trio’s fitness in massive boost to Mauricio Pochettino’s bid to preserve unique record appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
a02ac80a3857578c.content: On Sunday, Manchester United and Liverpool renew their rivalry at Anfield. Form-wise, everything suggests this is a game the hosts are more likely to win. United are enduring one of their worst starts to a Premier League campaign. After 10 games, they have won only once, picked up just eight points and sit 18th in the table, in the relegation zone. For their part, Liverpool have picked up 10 points more than United and are fourth in the league table with 18 points. The Andoni Iraola Anfield project seems to be gathering pace, with the Reds having lost only twice. Everything suggests a tough outing for United, but those on Merseyside are downplaying it. Liverpool have their worries about Manchester United’s visit Instead, they are quick to point to the advantages United hold going into this fixture, suggesting this game is a battle in itself. On Friday, Iraola was quick to point out the mystery of “which United they will face” on Sunday. With Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment and this being his first game in charge, it is unclear which tactics he will adopt, making the game trickier. Mauricio Pochettino managerial record Manager Seasons Club Played Won Drawn Lost Goals for Goals against Win % Mauricio Pochettino 2008/09–2012/13 RCD Espanyol Barcelona 161 53 38 70 184 218 32.9% Mauricio Pochettino 2012/13–2013/14 Southampton FC 60 23 18 19 87 73 38.3% Mauricio Pochettino 2014/15–2019/20 Tottenham Hotspur 293 160 60 73 559 322 54.6% Mauricio Pochettino 2020/21–2021/22 Paris Saint-Germain 84 56 13 15 196 87 66.7% Mauricio Pochettino 2023/24 Chelsea FC 51 27 10 14 107 76 52.9% Mauricio Pochettino 2024/25–2026/27 United States 37 24 1 12 81 51 64.9% Source: Wikipedia and API-Football Similarly, Ronald Araújo, speaking to The Athletic , echoes those comments and highlights the derby factor, despite United’s horrendous form. He confessed: “It doesn’t matter how the opposition are doing — a derby is always a derby. You draw on the extra energy you need. They’ve just changed their manager, and when there’s a change like that, the players might have some extra motivation. “It can be very difficult, but we’re focused on preparing in the best possible way. We’re playing at home, in front of our fans, and we’re going to go for the win.” Team news While Araújo has outlined those two factors, Liverpool’s injury issues could also leave them at a disadvantage. According to Premier Injuries , Conor Bradley, Hugo Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni are expected to miss this game. Jeremie Frimpong, Virgil van Dijk and Ryan Gravenberch, who all missed international duty through injury, are likely to be available. However, Premier Injuries report that the key Liverpool trio are not 100 per cent fit, which should work in United’s favour. For the Red Devils, Pochettino was set to face a tricky defensive selection. However, with Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire back in training in time for this game, the Argentine has a few ways to set up his defence and keep Liverpool at bay. So, as Iraola and Araújo suggest, Liverpool versus Man United will not be as easy as some thought. United, like Liverpool, have a chance of a famous win on Sunday evening. Fan fact: Pochettino has never lost his first match in charge of a club, a feat few managers can claim. db52b750403096a1.title: United midfield prodigy makes Pochettino’s faith count with jaw-dropping U18s goal
db52b750403096a1.text: Manchester United U18s fell to a 3-2 defeat against Derby County at Carrington despite goals from Kai Rooney and Jaume Camacho. The post Jaume Camacho continues hot form but it could not salvage a result for Man United U18s against Derby appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
db52b750403096a1.content: Manchester United U18s returned from the international break on Saturday morning, hosting Derby County at Carrington. Darren Fletcher’s side were bolstered by the return of Kai Rooney from suspension and looked to turn things around following a disappointing loss to Wolves last time out in the Premier League Cup. First half It was a poor start from the young Red Devils, though, which saw the visitors take the lead after just four minutes following a mistake by Yuel Helafu, which saw Derby deliver a low cross from the left into the area for Troy Ogedengbe to finish into the bottom corner. United almost produced a quick reply. Jaume Camacho’s side-footed effort following a pullback on the left wing was saved well by the Derby keeper. A series of chances came United’s way as they found their footing, but Camacho and Helafu came closest with efforts sailing just the wrong side of the woodwork. Jacob Watson was unlucky not to equalise in the 34th minute when his free-kick attempt struck the crossbar before crashing down and back up off the crossbar again before Derby’s Charlie Mountain punched the ball clear. At the other end, United’s Charlie Hardy, formerly with Derby, made a big save to stop Theo Olofingbuaro on the counter-attack. Despite United having the majority of the possession and chances, Derby doubled their lead in the 43rd minute when Jayden Ngwashi could do nothing but turn the ball into his own goal as Derby hit on the counter following a sloppy turnover in midfield by United. United kept themselves in the match going into the break, though, as Noah Ajayi burst past his marker before being tripped up to earn a penalty in stoppage time, which was dispatched by Kai Rooney . Second half The second half started as the first did, though, with Derby scoring another shortly after the restart. United were caught again on the counter-attack as Charlie Smith was found free on the right side of the area to poke past Hardy. Chances came United’s way, with Rafe McCormack forcing a good save before David Eze shot narrowly wide shortly after. United’s in-form man, Camacho, pulled the deficit back to one just before the hour mark with a sensational goal. Winning the ball on the left wing, he nutmegged the defender before dancing past another and lifting the ball over the keeper into the top-right corner. Camacho recently trained with the first-team under Mauricio Pochettino and has eight goals in his last four league matches for the U18s. Substitute Jay McEvoy came close with two efforts in quick succession, the first drawing a top save before the second went narrowly wide. Late chances came for Camacho, Ngwashi, and Ajayi, but none could find the net to salvage a point for United, who remain second in the table. Match facts United: Hardy; Helafu, Ngwashi, McCormack (c), J. Watson (Ziro 63); Eze (McEvoy 63), Cassim (Mpofu 88), Camacho; DeJonge-Seiros (O’Brien 63), Rooney, Ajayi. Unused subs: Ford, Laurie, Carrick. Goals: Rooney 45+1 (pen), Camacho 58. 2cd8a31c7703d9cc.title: Pochettino tipped to pursue familiar £35m-rated defender as his first Man United signing
2cd8a31c7703d9cc.text: Manchester United could revisit their interest in Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson as Mauricio Pochettino prepares for the January transfer window. The post Man United eye Fulham’s Antonee Robinson as Mauricio Pochettino’s first signing appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
2cd8a31c7703d9cc.content: Manchester United could target Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson as head coach Mauricio Pochettino’s first signing, with a January move said to be under consideration. United’s left-back search predates Pochettino Former head coach Michael Carrick guided United to third place last season, but he was dismissed on 12th November after collecting eight points from the opening 10 Premier League games of the new campaign. Pochettino was appointed the following day and began work on 18 November, with chief executive Omar Berrada later explaining the reasons behind the managerial change . Left-back was already an area of concern before the Argentine arrived. Luke Shaw has missed 10 matches in all competitions this season, forcing United to deploy centre-backs and right-backs out of position. Robinson subsequently emerged as a possible solution , while Lewis Hall, Malo Gusto, Rayan Aït-Nouri and Alejandro Balde have also been linked. Further reports claimed that United were preparing an opening offer of around £25 million, with Fulham seeking at least £35 million. Pochettino could turn to a familiar Fulham defender The 29-year-old worked under the new United head coach with the United States national team , a relationship said to have boosted the prospect of a move ( via Football Insider ). The report added: “Antonee Robinson has been a long-term target for United and obviously United do have issues at left back as well.” It continued: “And with Luke Shaw’s contract coming up to expire in the summer as well, they’re going to have to do something in that area to try and improve this team.” United are assessing multiple options for the position, having considered alternatives during the summer without completing a deal. Robinson could now be tempted to leave Fulham. “Robinson is somebody they have been looking at for a while, and if Pochettino wants to recruit some former players, he will be high on that list for him I’m sure,” reporter Peter O’Rourke said. Former United chief scout Mick Brown has also suggested that Pochettino could pursue players he previously coached. That pool includes members of his former United States squad and players from his spells at Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur, whom he already knows and can trust in his system. Several US internationals are reportedly being considered by United. With United 18th in the Premier League, Pochettino is believed to have identified key weaknesses he wants addressed during the winter window. Robinson’s route from Everton to Fulham Robinson entered Everton’s academy at the age of 11 and remained in the club’s development system between 2008 and 2017. He made his professional debut during a season-long loan at Bolton Wanderers in 2017/18, recording 30 appearances. After initially joining Wigan Athletic on loan, Robinson completed a permanent move in 2019. He made 64 league appearances for the Latics overall before Fulham signed him for approximately £2 million on 20 August 2020. The defender signed a new Fulham contract in July 2023 running until June 2028. He was named the club’s Player of the Year for 2023/24 and became the first defender since 2006 to win the US Soccer Male Player of the Year award in 2024. Robinson has registered five goals in 63 senior appearances for the United States. The Peoples Person Reliability Assessment Overall credibility: 3/10 Why? Everything in the report is logical. We don’t trust Football Insider as a source. TPP view Robinson is an obvious name to throw in the mix but it does not seem like a long-term solution for United.
